properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 5:58PM MDT until July 31 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Luna County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 558 PM MDT, Slow moving thunderstorms near Waterloo have
produced over an inch of rain in less than an hour. Storms are
beginning to drift south towards the Tres Hermanas mountains,
which drains into the same area.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of arroyos and streams, roads, and as
well as other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Waterloo, areas along Seventy Six Draw, including portions of
Montezuma Road and Inmon Ranch Road.

If rainfall continues, portions of State Highway 11 may be impacted.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 31 at 5:49PM MDT until July 31 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 549 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 12
miles east of Logan to 12 miles north of House, moving southeast at
30 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Surface observations. The Tucumcari Airport reported a wind
gust of 72 mph at 537 PM MDT.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect considerable
tree damage. Wind damage is also likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Tucumcari, Quay, Logan, San Jon, Grady, House, Wheatland, Ragland,
Broadview and Bellview.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 40 between Mile Markers 332 and 373. Highway 60 between
Mile Markers 358 and 359.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. These storms have produced widespread
damaging winds and are capable of producing large hail.

Blowing dust associated with strong thunderstorm winds can reduce
visibility below one quarter mile at times.

properties.description:

rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Alpena, Ossineke, Hubbard Lake, Ossineke Township, Spruce, Spratt,

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1100 PM CDT for south central
Missouri.

Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 5:55PM MDT until July 31 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 555 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain have moved southeast of the North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn
Scar. Between 0.1 and 0.7 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
storms may be moving into the western edge of the burn scar around
630 PM.  Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow. The
debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the North and Middle Aspen
Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah and San Isabel.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Middle Creek, North Creek, Squirrel Creek, Willow Creek, North Red
Creek, and South Hardscrabble Creek.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the North and Middle Aspen Acres Burn Scar. Severe debris flows
can also be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be
washed away in places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to
safety.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 2:30PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 38.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight into the early morning hours on
Saturday. The river is then expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, Major flooding below Cotulla to below
Tilden occurs, and cuts off extensive portions of the flood plain,
requiring wholesale evacuation of livestock from the area. Roads
and bridges near the river flood severely. Hunting cabins, pump
jacks, tank batteries, irrigation pumps and any equipment in low
areas near the river flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 20.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Sunday evening, falling to 16.1 feet early Wednesday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
